title: DB migration CI check: run every migration-* compose service, report per-service results, fail the step if any failed
answers: Why does the master CI migration check fail with only a generic exit code instead of naming the database that broke?
How do I add a new migration service (e.g. another database backend) so the CI migration check picks it up?
Where is the CI step that runs the database migration checks for each backend handled?
Why did the migration check keep going after one database failed, and how does it decide the overall job result?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/master.yml, the "Run migration check" step in the database job. It runs `./tests/db/compose.sh down --volumes --remove-orphans`, then loops over `./tests/db/compose.sh config --services | grep '^migration-'` and runs `compose.sh run --rm --no-TTY` for each service (e.g. migration-mssql, migration-postgres).
Rule: Every `migration-*` service runs even when an earlier one fails. Each service's exit status is recorded in a `results` array ("name: ✅" or "name: ❌ (exit code N)"), a `::error::` annotation naming the service and exit code is emitted on failure, the summary is printed with `printf`, and the step ends with `exit "$failed"`. New migration backends are picked up automatically by the `^migration-` service-name prefix, so name new services with that prefix.
Symptom: A failed migration job showed only a generic step exit code. Diagnosing it meant reading logs to find that migration-mssql had timed out, and later services were not reported at all once an earlier one aborted the loop.
Constraints: Applies to the CI migration check in master.yml only. Do not reintroduce `set +e` with an ERR trap or a `test $err = 0` tail; that pattern hides which service failed. This does not change how an individual migration service runs or its compose definition in tests/db.
applies: CI workflow for database migration checks in .github/workflows/master.yml; not the migrations themselves or the compose files.
says: The database migration pipeline fails with a generic error without naming the broken database.
Continuous integration stops testing remaining database migrations when an earlier database check fails.
Automated migration checks should display individual pass or fail status for every database.
Show clear error annotations identifying which database backend timed out during migration testing.
search: In .github/workflows/master.yml, the database migration check step runs every compose service matching '^migration-' using tests/db/compose.sh, continuing execution even when individual services fail. The step records per-service exit statuses in a results array, emits a GitHub Actions '::error::' annotation with the service name and exit code for failures, prints a summary, and exits with the failure count. New database migration backends are automatically discovered by prefixing service names with 'migration-'. This workflow-level rule applies only to master.yml, avoiding 'set +e' with ERR traps or 'test $err = 0' patterns, and does not alter compose definitions in tests/db.
